key_insight: Transporting a log-concave source to heavy-tailed or well-separated multimodal targets intrinsically requires large gradients, regardless of neural architecture or training procedure.
engineering_relevance: Pushforward generative models face expressivity–numerical stability trade-offs when representing heavy tails or separated modes.
method: Derive quantitative lower bounds on transport gradients and Jacobians.
Establish results under weaker regularity assumptions and target perturbations.
Propose bijective reparametrizations to reduce gradient demands for density approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments support the theoretical analysis, but the abstract provides no datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative results.
watch_item: The proposed mitigation concerns density approximation and should not be assumed to remove barriers in generative sampling.
paper_title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
